install.manual_review: Review the target, baseline, network, credential, and approval boundaries before enabling any host adapter.

source_boundary: The selected paths were clean in the primary checkout; install-contract execution used a clean archive at the recorded commit. Recovery execution used that same archive plus the local recovery patch to scripts/workbench.py (patch SHA-256 8441feb51f6f68eb5c2aa39f79b99cd240c98b20eb4d70994320c9f35a753340); unrelated work remained outside the evidence source.
fixture_strategy: Use the real public manifest entry and tracked contract files. Run the documented installer in two empty target roots, compare sanitized statuses, inventories, and hashes, then run receipt-scoped uninstall in both targets with an unrelated sentinel and a modified-file guard. Do not treat copied text contracts as proof of host registration or runtime behavior.

environments.provider_difference: none at the portable file projection; host registration remains manual
Codex is a supported target, but the Codex adapter is not registered by installation

required_behaviors.statement: dry_run: true produces a plan and performs no mutation.
A target outside the declared scope is rejected before execution.
Existing files are not overwritten unless a separately reviewed policy allows it.
Hook and configuration changes are staged for review, never registered as an installation side effect.
The result records status, actions, verification, and partial_failures.
Receipt-scoped uninstall removes only recorded files whose contents still match and refuses modified or unowned targets.

open_boundaries: The two projections prove install-contract parity, not provider runtime behavior or host registration.
PW-4 runtime equivalence was attempted and is blocked: generic has no executable host, Codex provider execution is not permitted, and no local OSS provider is installed.
claim_boundary: This case proves public manifest selection, non-mutating previews, explicit copies, overwrite refusal, byte-identical generic/Codex portable projections, and receipt-scoped recovery that preserves unrelated files and blocks modified targets. It records an attempted but blocked runtime comparison; it does not prove model quality, host registration, provider runtime behavior, credentials, network access, or host-runtime equivalence.
